record_body:
Overview
- Product: customer support platform (agent assist). Primary workflow is real-time chat + suggested replies + short summaries that get logged into the ticket.
- Why Redwood: need consistent streaming performance + operational controls (routing/fallback) without building/operating their own GPU stack.

Current stage: Evaluation / POC
- POC is live in a sandbox environment behind feature flag for ~25 agents. Goal is to expand to 200+ agents if stability holds.

Use case details (support-agent)
- Interaction pattern: streaming chat completion for suggested replies; post-chat summary generation per conversation; light classification (intent/priority) for routing.
- Traffic shape: bursty during shift changes and incident events. Spikes are the norm; they want predictable degradation instead of hard failures.
- Latency targets (stated):
  - Suggested reply: p95 time-to-first-token < 500ms, p95 completion < 3.5s for typical turns.
  - Summary: p95 < 6s acceptable (non-blocking).
- Reliability: target <0.2% error rate during peak; “timeouts are worse than slower answers.”

Routing + fallback requirements (key)
- Must support automated fallback on:
  - 429/rate-limit conditions
  - upstream model saturation / elevated queue times
  - region-level blips
- Fallback policy preference (their words): “degrade gracefully to a smaller model that is always available,” especially for suggested replies.
- Want separate policies by route:
  - /agent_reply: prioritize latency; allow more aggressive fallback
  - /summary: prioritize cost; OK to queue/batch
- Interested in canary rollout + quick revert for model version changes (prior regressions in other providers).

Security / compliance notes
- SOC 2 package requested (standard). SSO/SAML preferred for Console access.
- Data handling: customer support transcripts may include PII; they are pushing for configurable retention controls and audit logs for admin actions.
- No strict residency requirement mentioned yet, but their procurement team asked where inference runs (region transparency).

POC notes & issues
- Streaming stability issues observed in POC (disconnects / timeouts) during peak replay tests.
  - Jira: SUP-2410_heliosupport_streaming_timeouts_during_poc
  - Actioned: tuning rate limits, reviewing client retry behavior, and testing alternate streaming settings.
- Customer feedback: content quality is “good enough” vs current baseline; the gating item is reliability under load.

Metrics / validation approach (in progress)
- Plan: traffic replay over 7-day window with known peak periods.
- Need to lock measurement definitions for publishing/claims (even internally): p50/p95 latency, error rate (timeout vs 429), and throughput at peak.
- Simran + Logan to confirm telemetry alignment and what can be screenshot/published (most likely internal-only).

Reference program potential
- Likely reference-call candidate (not public case study yet).
- Customer stance: willing to do 1:1 calls with qualified prospects if we keep topics bounded (no volumes, no exact $/token, no detailed vendor comparisons).
- Candidate champions (customer-side):
  - Maya Patel — Director, Support Operations (business sponsor; cares about agent productivity and response speed)
  - Kenji Tanaka — Staff ML Engineer (technical sponsor; cares about routing/fallback + rollout controls)
  - Erin Walsh — Security/Compliance Manager (approval gate for anything external)
- Internal note: if POC stabilizes + Dedicated sizing is clear, this could become a strong “reliability + graceful degradation” reference.

Activity timeline (recent)
- 2025-05-15 — POC scoping call (Fireflies: ff_2025-05-15_heliosupport_poc-scoping). Aligned on streaming targets + fallback must-haves.
- 2025-05-21 — Initial integration completed (SDK + streaming). Early agent feedback positive on speed.
- 2025-05-29 — Peak replay test surfaced intermittent timeouts; opened SUP-2410.
- 2025-06-03 — POC check-in (Fireflies: ff_2025-06-03_heliosupport_poc-checkin). Reviewed mitigations: rate limits, retry strategy, and fallback configuration by route.

Open questions
- Do they want Dedicated for peak hours only or full-time reserved capacity?
- Confirm whether they need audit log export format (fields + cadence) similar to Arcadia’s asks, or just Console-level audit trails.
- Decide reference participation level: reference-call-only vs anonymized write-up.

Deal notes
- If we can demonstrate stable streaming + clean fallback behavior under load, budget is pre-approved for an annual commit in the stated ARR range.
- Procurement will want a short addendum around retention controls + audit log availability; keep legal looped in once POC passes acceptance tests.
